+# Combined report: Q1, Q2 and Q4
+
+This document concatenates the three original question reports as text for group review.
+The imported scientific claims were not rewritten, reassigned, or revalidated, so this merged file is a convenience copy rather than a rewrite.
+The only integration change inside each text is that relative link targets are prefixed with `questions/qN/` so figures and data links resolve from the repository root, and Markdown image embeds that point to `.html` figures became normal links because HTML cannot be embedded as an image.
+
+# Q1 Implied Volatility Surface of China Index Options
+
+## 1. Executive summary
+
+This project estimates China CSI 300 option implied-volatility surfaces using public CFFEX historical contract data. Approach 1 performs quote filtering, Black–Scholes inversion, put–call parity diagnostics, constrained SVI calibration, repricing, and no-arbitrage checks. Approach 2 compares differentiable PyTorch SVI calibration with SciPy and trains a price-space neural surface with butterfly/calendar penalties. The liquid quote pipeline retains 225 quotes, successfully inverts 224, fits 12 SVI groups, obtains zero butterfly-grid violations, and has 1.67% median liquid-strike repricing error. Under a 30% quote-drop experiment, SVI obtains 0.067% median relative price error on held-out quotes and the neural surface obtains 0.204%.
+
+## 2. Data and provenance
+
+The data pipeline uses the assignment-approved `akshare` interfaces: `option_cffex_hs300_spot_sina` and `option_cffex_hs300_daily_sina` for contract strikes and daily OHLCV, `stock_zh_index_daily(symbol="sh000300")` for the CSI 300 index, and `macro_china_shibor_all` for the historical 3M SHIBOR rate. The snapshot contains nine expiry months, 1,134 raw call/put quote rows, 177 observed dates, and a date range from 2023-03-20 to 2026-01-13. A shared October 2023 block contains four expiries on five dates, enabling calendar diagnostics.
+
+For every selected contract, the fetcher keeps the first five trading dates within a 31-calendar-day window and 13 evenly spaced strikes. It also keeps a common 2023-10-23 through 2023-10-27 block for four overlapping expiries when the contract traded on those dates. Raw responses are cached in ignored `data/raw/`; clean snapshots and SHA-256 hashes are committed in `data/clean/metadata.json`.
+
+The formal liquid-quote rule is volume at least 40 and forward moneyness `0.9 <= K/F <= 1.1`. The rule is declared before calibration and is exposed through CLI parameters. The underlying dividend yield is set to zero because the primary instrument is the CSI 300 index option rather than an ETF; this assumption is a limitation and is not hidden.
+
+## 3. Market definitions
+
+For quote date `t`, spot `S`, continuously compounded rate `r`, time to expiry `T`, and zero dividend yield, the forward is
+
+\[
+F=S e^{rT}, \qquad D=e^{-rT}.
+\]
+
+For volatility `sigma`,
+
+\[
+d_1=\frac{\log(F/K)+\frac12\sigma^2T}{\sigma\sqrt{T}},
+\qquad d_2=d_1-\sigma\sqrt{T}.
+\]
+
+The Black–Scholes forward prices are
+
+\[
+C=D(FN(d_1)-KN(d_2)),
+\qquad P=D(KN(-d_2)-FN(-d_1)).
+\]
+
+Implied volatility is obtained separately for every call and put using bracketed Brent root finding on `[10^-4, 5]`. Five of 225 filtered quotes fail the admissible price bracket and are reported as divergence cases rather than silently removed.
+
+Put–call parity is evaluated as
+
+\[
+\epsilon_{PC}=C-P-(S-Ke^{-rT}).
+\]
+
+There are 166 matched strike groups after filtering. The mean residual is 0.0165 index points, RMSE is 14.4405, and the 95th percentile absolute residual is 19.0721. The large dispersion is retained as a data-quality finding because daily closes are not executable bid/ask mids.
+
+## 4. Approach 1: classical market pipeline
+
+For each date/expiry group, total variance is `w(k)=sigma_IV^2 T` and log-moneyness is `k=log(K/F)`. SVI is
+
+\[
+w(k)=a+b\left[\rho(k-m)+\sqrt{(k-m)^2+\eta^2}\right],
+\]
+
+with `b >= 0`, `|rho| < 1`, and `eta > 0`. The implementation first obtains a bounded least-squares initialization and then uses SLSQP with inequality constraints `g(k)>=0` on an 81-point interior grid. The objective remains squared total-variance error; constraint failure is reported.
+
+The Gatheral butterfly diagnostic is
+
+\[
+g(k)=\left(1-\frac{kw'(k)}{2w(k)}\right)^2-
+\frac{w'(k)^2}{4}\left(\frac1{w(k)}+\frac14\right).
+\]
+
+Calendar checks compare fitted total variance at the same `k` for increasing expiries. Forward variance is the finite difference of total variance divided by the maturity difference. The surface is delivered on an 81-point fixed grid in `results/approach1/market/surface_grid.csv`.
+
+### 4.1 Results
+
+| Quantity | Result |
+|---|---:|
+| Filtered quotes | 225 |
+| Successful IV quotes | 224 |
+| SVI groups | 12 |
+| IV divergence cases | 1 |
+| Butterfly violations | 0 |
+| Calendar violations | 20 |
+| Negative forward-variance locations | 20 |
+| Median repricing relative error | 1.67% |
+| 95th percentile of group p95 repricing | 39.21% |
+
+Calendar and forward-variance violations occur on 2023-10-23 and 2023-10-24; they are counted and located in `metrics.json`. No violations are silently dropped. The high group-level p95 is consistent with sparse daily close data and is discussed as a limitation.
+
+[SVI surface](questions/q1/results/approach1/market/svi_surface.html)
+
+[Arbitrage diagnostics](questions/q1/results/approach1/market/arbitrage_diagnostics.html)
+
+## 5. Approach 2: differentiable calibration
+
+### 5.1 Differentiable SVI
+
+The PyTorch SVI implementation uses reparameterization:
+
+\[
+a=\operatorname{softplus}(u_a),\quad b=\operatorname{softplus}(u_b),\quad
+\rho=0.999\tanh(u_\rho),\quad \eta=\operatorname{softplus}(u_\eta).
+\]
+
+Adam runs for 300 epochs on each of the 12 groups. The mean SciPy objective is `1.97e-08`, while the mean Torch objective is `1.97e-08`; mean wall time is 0.0087 seconds for SciPy and 0.0374 seconds for Torch on this small dataset. This comparison separates optimizer overhead from statistical fit quality.
+
+### 5.2 Neural surface
+
+The neural surface is an MLP with two hidden tanh layers and a positive softplus volatility output. Inputs are `(k,T)`. The loss is normalized option-price squared error plus arbitrage penalties:
+
+\[
+\mathcal L=\operatorname{MSE}\left(\frac{\hat C-C_{mkt}}{F}\right)
+ +\lambda_b\operatorname{mean}[\max(0,-g(k))^2]
+ +\lambda_T\operatorname{mean}[\max(0,-\partial_Tw)^2].
+\]
+
+The ablation grid is `(lambda_b,lambda_T)` in `{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)}`. All four trained surfaces have zero grid-level butterfly and calendar violations; their median in-sample relative price error is 0.173%. The equality of the ablation results is itself informative: the filtered training region was already smooth enough that the penalties were inactive.
+
+### 5.3 Robustness
+
+Thirty percent of liquid quotes are randomly dropped with seed 42. The remaining 156 quotes train the models and 68 independent dropped quotes form the evaluation set.
+
+| Model | Median relative error | P95 relative error |
+|---|---:|---:|
+| SVI refit | 0.067% | 0.182% |
+| Neural surface | 0.204% | 0.941% |
+
+The SVI refit is more accurate on this small, structured snapshot, while the neural model provides a smooth differentiable surface and remains competitive under missing quotes.
+
+[Differentiable calibration](questions/q1/results/approach2/differentiable/svi_convergence.html)
+
+[Neural ablation](questions/q1/results/approach2/differentiable/neural_ablation.html)
+
+## 6. Reproducibility and validation
+
+The environment is Python 3.13 with dependencies pinned in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. The default seed is 42. The canonical commands are:
+
+```bash
+uv sync
+python data/fetch.py --seed 42
+python code/approach1_market_pipeline.py --seed 42
+python code/approach2_differentiable.py --seed 42
+python code/compare.py
+```
+
+Both approaches expose `argparse` CLIs, write the required `metrics.json` schema, use self-contained Plotly HTML, and preserve quote filtering, divergence cases, parity residuals, no-arbitrage counts, convergence information, and dropout results.
+
+## 7. Limitations
+
+The source supplies daily OHLCV closes rather than synchronized bid/ask mids, so parity residuals and repricing tails reflect stale and asynchronous quotes. Zero dividend yield is a simplifying assumption. The snapshot uses a manageable set of CFFEX contracts rather than every listed ETF chain. The calendar block has only a few overlapping expiry dates after the strict liquidity filter, which is why calendar violations are reported as diagnostics rather than interpreted as a definitive market-arbitrage claim. A production surface would use bid/ask intervals, dividend forecasts, more contracts, and constrained price-space calibration across all maturities.
+
+## 8. Division of work
+
+The terminal workflow implemented the data retrieval, checksum metadata, numerical estimators, constrained calibration, neural calibration, robustness experiments, figures, and reproducibility scaffolding. The group is responsible for reviewing assumptions, checking the mathematics, approving the quote filter and dividend convention, and making final claims.
+

+# Q2. Monte Carlo pricing and hedging on Chinese futures
+
+I first checked that the simulator could reproduce a Black-Scholes price.
+Then I used the same daily grid to compare pricing estimators and test whether the learned hedge reduced losses after trading costs.
+
+## Data and setup
+
+I used daily IF0 and CU0 futures closes from Sina Finance, the CSI 300 cash index from Eastmoney, and SHIBOR fixings from Jin10, all retrieved through AKShare.
+The calibration window was January 2, 2020 through December 31, 2025, with 1,455 closes and 1,454 log returns per contract.
+The loader verifies the committed snapshots against the [data manifest](questions/q2/data/metadata.json).
+The CSI 300 cash index is a reference series.
+The model inputs come from the futures closes.
+
+For daily log returns $x_t=\log(S_t/S_{t-1})$, I estimated annualized volatility as $\hat\sigma=\sqrt{252}\,s_x$ and historical GBM drift as $\hat\mu=252\,\bar x+\hat\sigma^2/2$.
+
+| Contract | Last close | Annual volatility | Annual GBM drift |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| IF0 | 4,599.80 | 20.31% | 3.80% |
+| CU0 | 98,240.00 | 17.87% | 13.57% |
+
+I valued the options on December 31, 2025 with a one-year maturity.
+I interpolate SHIBOR simple quotes by tenor and convert the selected quote $q$ to $r=\log(1+qT)/T$.
+The one-year fixing of 1.65% gives $r=1.6365\%$.
+Under the assignment's pricing model, each daily step is
+
+$$
+S_{i+1}=S_i\exp\!\left[(r-\hat\sigma^2/2)\Delta t+\hat\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}\,Z_i\right],
+\qquad Z_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1).
+$$
+
+Both engines use 252 steps, 100,000 paths for pricing, and seed 42 with separate random streams.
+The strike is $K=S_0$.
+The arithmetic Asian pays $(\bar S-K)^+$, averaging the 252 observations after time zero.
+The up-and-out pays $(S_T-K)^+$ if the price stays below $1.5S_0$ at every monitoring date, with zero rebate.
+The digital pays one unit if $S_T>K$.
+All prices are discounted sample means.
+

+I used a short at-the-money European call for the hedge comparison because it has an exact Black-Scholes delta.
+The PyTorch engine also prices the three exotic options above.
+The hedge is a one-hidden-layer MLP with 16 units, tanh activation, and a sigmoid output, taking $S_t/S_0$ and $t$ as inputs.
+I used the assignment's terminal P&L, with gains accrued to expiry, the fee charged on each change in position including entry, and the call payoff deducted at maturity.

+$$
+V_T=\sum_j e^{r(T-t_j)}\Delta_j(S_{t_{j+1}}-S_{t_j})

+# Q4 China Financial and Trade Networks
+
+## 1. Executive summary
+
+This project studies an annual directed trade network induced by China’s largest trade partners from 2014–2023. Approach 1 measures network structure, minimum spanning trees, Louvain communities, centrality, and temporal migration. Approach 2 implements node2vec with biased walks, skip-gram negative sampling, a learned bilinear link scorer, and three heuristic baselines. On the fixed 2023 held-out split, the best embedding configuration (`p=2`, `q=0.5`, dimension 64) reaches AUC 0.810 and average precision 0.847, compared with AUC 0.750 for preferential attachment, 0.745 for common neighbors, and 0.705 for Adamic–Adar.
+
+## 2. Data and network construction
+
+The source is the keyless UN Comtrade preview API specified by the assignment. `data/fetch.py` first ranks partners by China’s latest anchor-year imports plus exports, selects 20 partners, and fixes the node set to China plus those partners for every year. It then retrieves reported exports for every induced reporter–partner pair. The committed clean snapshot contains 10 years, 21 country nodes, and 4,160 positive raw edge rows. Raw API responses are cached under the ignored `data/raw/` directory; `data/clean/metadata.json` records the retrieval timestamp, schema, source, and SHA-256 hashes.
+
+For year `t`, the raw directed edge is
+
+\[
+T_{ij,t}=\text{primaryValue}_{ij,t},
+\]
+
+measured in USD. Because all selected countries report some small positive bilateral flows, the unfiltered induced graph is nearly complete and cannot support equal negative sampling. The analysis graph therefore keeps the six largest export edges per reporter per year. This rule is fixed before evaluation, is applied identically across years, and leaves the unfiltered clean snapshot available for audit. Self-loops are excluded by construction and checked in every run.
+
+The assignment’s stock-industry labels are not defined for country nodes. We therefore use geographical region as a clearly labelled proxy only for community comparison; the primary Q4-B task is held-out trade-edge recovery rather than industry prediction.
+
+## 3. Reproducibility
+
+The environment is Python 3.13 with dependencies pinned in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. The global default seed is 42. The canonical commands are:
+
+```bash
+uv sync
+python data/fetch.py --seed 42
+python code/approach1_network_analytics.py --seed 42 --top-k 6
+python code/approach2_node_embeddings.py --seed 42 --top-k 6
+python code/compare.py
+```
+
+Each approach uses the required CLI, writes `results/approachN/trade/metrics.json` with `params`, `metrics`, `fit_seconds`, and `history`, and writes self-contained Plotly HTML figures.
+
+## 4. Approach 1: network analytics
+
+The directed graph is converted to an undirected weighted graph by summing reciprocal export weights. The metric used for the Kruskal minimum spanning tree is
+
+\[
+d_{ij}=\frac{1}{\log(1+w_{ij})},
+\]
+
+so larger trade relationships have shorter distances. We report node count, edge count, density, mean degree, a log–log degree-frequency slope, assortativity, connected components, isolated nodes, and self-loops. Louvain maximizes the weighted modularity
+
+\[
+Q=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{ij}\left(A_{ij}-\frac{k_i k_j}{2m}\right)\mathbf{1}(c_i=c_j).
+\]
+
+PageRank uses damping 0.85. Betweenness uses shortest paths, and weighted degree sums trade values. Resolution sensitivity is evaluated at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5. Consecutive-year migration is reported as an aligned contingency matrix and ARI.

+## 5. Approach 2: node2vec and link prediction
+
+For a walk with previous node `t`, current node `v`, and candidate next node `x`, the node2vec transition bias is
+
+\[
+\alpha_{pq}(t,x)=
+\begin{cases}
+1/p & x=t,\\
+1 & (t,x)\in E,\\
+1/q & \text{otherwise},
+\end{cases}
+\]
+
+multiplied by the observed edge weight before normalization. Walk contexts use a window of two. The skip-gram objective uses positive context pairs and five uniformly sampled negative contexts:
+
+\[
+\log\sigma(z_v^\top c_u)+\sum_{r=1}^{5}\log\sigma(-z_v^\top c_{n_r}).
+\]
+
+The final-year graph is split into 80/10/10 positive edges and an equal number of negative non-edges: 72/9/10 in train/validation/test. The learned link score is
+
+\[
+s(u,v)=\sigma(z_u^\top Wz_v),
+\]
+
+where `W` is fitted only on the training split. Baselines are common neighbors, Adamic–Adar, and preferential attachment. We report AUC, average precision, and k-means agreement with Louvain and the region proxy using ARI/NMI.
+

+At the best configuration, average precision is 0.847. Embedding clusters have ARI 0.069 and NMI 0.249 against Louvain, and ARI 0.016 and NMI 0.293 against the region proxy. Thus the embedding is more useful for edge recovery than for reproducing the classical community partition.

+## 6. Limitations and checks
+
+The preview API provides reported values and does not guarantee a complete reconciled world trade matrix. The fixed 21-node induced network is intentionally manageable and is not a full global network. The top-k rule improves link-prediction identifiability but changes the interpretation from all reported flows to major relationships. Country regions are not industry labels, so region agreement is explicitly a proxy rather than evidence of industry alignment. The test set is small; AUC and AP are reported together and should not be overinterpreted. Future work would use a larger country universe, multiple HS levels, repeated temporal test windows, and bootstrap uncertainty intervals.
+
+## 7. Division of work
+
+The terminal workflow implemented the data retrieval, checksum metadata, graph construction, estimators, benchmarks, figures, and reproducibility scaffolding. Q2 compares Monte Carlo estimators and transaction-cost hedges on a GBM model calibrated from Chinese futures data.

 # MQF Advanced Programming project contract
 
 ## Objective
 
 Complete both approaches for each experiment in one reproducible repository with the questions Q1, Q2 and Q4 integrated under `questions/`.
 Q1 builds a volatility-surface pipeline with a classical market-data approach and a differentiable-quantitative-finance counterpart.
 Q2 compares Monte Carlo estimators and transaction-cost hedges on a GBM model calibrated from Chinese futures data.
 Q4 compares classical graph analytics and learned embeddings on a Chinese trade network.
 The group owns the mathematical choices, verifies the results, and writes the report.
 Confirm any methodological ambiguity with the group before making it part of the experiment.
 
 ## Question isolation and environments
 
 Each question lives in its own folder `questions/qN/` with its own `code/`, `data/`, `results/`, `README.md`, `report.md`, `SESSION.md`, `pyproject.toml` and pinned `uv.lock`.
 Question-specific dependency versions are unchanged and each question runs in its own locked environment.
 Do not merge question requirements or upgrade their pins centrally.
 Scientific scripts, manifests, committed snapshots, saved metrics, saved figures and original sessions are preserved and must not be edited from the root.
 Run every scientific script with its working directory set to the question directory so question-local packages such as `common.py` or a `code/` package cannot collide.
 
 ## Environment and commands
 
 Use the root launcher `run.py` (standard library only) to verify snapshots and execute each question's scripts in fresh subprocesses with isolated uv environments.
 
 ```sh
 python3 run.py all --stage verify
 python3 run.py q2 --offline
 python3 run.py all --offline
 ```
 
 The launcher CLI is `python3 run.py {q1,q2,q4,all} [--stage {verify,approach1,approach2,compare,all,index}] [--seed 42] [--offline] [--dry-run]`.
 Every execution stage verifies the committed snapshots first, except `--dry-run` which only prints plans.
 Verification uses stdlib hashes only, with no uv, no third-party imports and no vendor fetchers.

 Inside a question you can still run its own documented commands from that question's directory using its locked lockfile.
 
 ## Data and experiments
 
 Commit offline fallback snapshots for every external source used.
 Each question records source, query, retrieval date, schema, and SHA-256 in its `data/metadata.json` (Q2) or `data/clean/metadata.json` (Q1/Q4) manifests.
